title: The Spark Artifact stores the Encumbrance Ratio target in two places and mandates manual synchronization
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.1.3 states the target and then states the hazard in the same breath: "This parameter will be maintained in parallel with the value specified in the Spark Artifact Allocation System Primitive section at A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.3.1...; **any change to one section of the Spark Artifact will require a corresponding change in the other section**."

The Artifact is thus knowingly holding one value twice, with correctness depending on whoever drafts a future amendment remembering the twin. There is no single source of truth and no mechanism enforcing the coupling — only a sentence asking for it.

This is notable because the Atlas elsewhere avoids exactly this. Cross-references are the dominant idiom throughout the document: definitions live in one place and are linked from everywhere else, right down to individual parameter definitions being their own subdocuments. The tooling to point at the value instead of copying it plainly exists and is used constantly.

Why it was duplicated is not stated, but the effect is a class of error the rest of the structure is designed to prevent. A governance process that changes the Allocation System section's target and not this one produces an Artifact that contradicts itself on Spark's central solvency constraint, and both readings would be equally authoritative text.

The honest reading is that the clause is a documented compromise, not an oversight — the drafters saw the duplication, could not or would not restructure, and wrote the invariant down where a future editor might see it. That is better than silence, and materially worse than a reference.
description: The parameter 'will be maintained in parallel' with a copy in the Allocation System Primitive section, with any change to one requiring a corresponding change to the other.
